clue.text: If coming back to stay, you may get warm here

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so the little word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, before it is turned round
to reside somewhere is to stay there

explanation.surface: A host promising a cosy spot to a guest who decides to come back and stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If coming back' looks like a condition on the guest, but only the little word If is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The area around a domestic hearth is where people sit to heat themselves, so it is a place you get warm.

clue.text: Dictator's father a corporal perhaps

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
taken as written
a corporal is one example of a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A dictator's own dad was only a lowly corporal in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Franco ruled Spain as an authoritarian leader from 1939 until his death in 1975.

clue.text: No good growing tiny fruit

indicators.note: saying no to something means doing without it, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: raising crops is growing them
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A gardener complaining that the small fruit is not growing well.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the G out of RAISING to leave RAISIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, shrunken and small, so it is a little piece of fruit.

clue.text: One's bowled over by girl presented with large teapots and hair extensions

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked head over heels, so the short phrase is read backwards

parts.note: one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I + S, which then turns round
a deb, short for debutante, is a young society girl
urns are large vessels for serving tea to a crowd; presented with just joins them on

explanation.surface: Someone is bowled over by a girl serving tea from huge urns while sporting hair extensions.
explanation.walkthrough: IS reversed gives SI, then DEB and URNS make SIDEBURNS. A deb is a debutante, a young woman making her entrance into high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair that extend down the side of a man's face in front of the ears.

clue.text: No wild-eyed hot revolutionary!

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these three words is the raw material

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a stolid, conventional person: certainly no fiery radical.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: someone dyed-in-the-wool holds fixed, settled views, the opposite of a wild-eyed revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed-in-the-wool describes someone thoroughly set in their ways, an entrenched traditionalist rather than a hothead who wants upheaval.

clue.text: Committee men don't have a month to fill desirable job

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so these letters sit within the job

parts.note: a plum job is a highly desirable one

indicators.note: not having something means it is missing, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its M
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Men on a committee missing out on a month's work in a sought-after post.
explanation.walkthrough: A plum job is British slang for a cushy, much-coveted post.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a full meeting of an assembly or committee, with all members present.

clue.text: Playful law lord sick at heart

parts.note: lud is how a judge is addressed in court, as in 'm'lud', a form of lord

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A senior judge who is playful but feeling sick inside.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts barristers address a judge as 'my lord', slurred to 'm'lud', so LUD stands for a law lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludic comes from the Latin for play and describes behaviour that is spontaneous and full of fun.

clue.text: Poison several crowding one bed

indicators.note: to crowd something is to press in around it, so the number surrounds the other letters

parts.note: nine stands for an unspecified number, several
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Something poisonous with too many people crammed into a single bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Using a specific number for 'several' is a loose but common crossword liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the toxic alkaloid in tobacco, highly poisonous in a concentrated dose.

clue.text: Street's manifest disuse under motorway entrance to Indian reservations

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming below it, so these pieces follow the others

parts.note: M is the prefix of British motorway numbers, like the M1

indicators.note: the entrance is where you go in, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter
St is the abbreviation for street
rust shows that metal has stood unused for a long time

explanation.surface: A neglected road running beneath a motorway on the way into an Indian reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'under' puts ST and RUST beneath M and I. 'Indian reservations' looks like one phrase, but reservations alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservations are doubts or misgivings, so having them about someone is a feeling of suspicion or distrust.

clue.text: Aid near perhaps for woman abandoned on Greek island

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given are only one possible arrangement, so they are reordered

parts.note: the raw letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether help is close at hand for a woman marooned on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Theseus left Ariadne behind on Naxos after she helped him escape the Minotaur's labyrinth.

clue.text: Governing, takes risks showing symbols of power

parts.note: a party that is in is in power, governing
to dice, as in dice with death, is to take risks

explanation.surface: A ruling party gambling to show off the trappings of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Symbols of power' suggests crowns and sceptres; in mathematics it means exponents.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an index is the small raised number showing the power to which a quantity is raised.

clue.text: Vital, but not to be had from chemist?

definitions.text: not to be had from chemist?
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: split as IN plus a word for what a pharmacist can hand over, with IN meaning not

explanation.walkthrough: A chemist is a British pharmacist, who dispenses medicines; the question mark flags reading the answer as 'not dispensable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential cannot be done without, and read literally the word also says it cannot be handed out by a pharmacist.

clue.text: Start to cover leg and shin up

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening, so just the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Instructions to protect your leg and shin before starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shin' looks like part of the leg, but 'shin up' is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shin up a tree or rope is to ascend it quickly using hands and legs.

clue.text: To lay a charge, soldiers receive a sign

indicators.note: something that receives takes another thing in, so a letter goes inside the combined word

parts.note: to indict someone is to formally charge them
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops being given a signal before laying an explosive charge.
explanation.walkthrough: INDICT and OR join, then take in A.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is something that points to or signals a condition, so it is a sign.

clue.text: Inspiring figure's French art includes later 'Man with Sieve'

indicators.note: a word that includes another holds it inside, so the time word sits within the rest

parts.note: Erato is one of the Muses, who inspire poets; the 's gives the S
es is French for 'art', as in the old English 'thou art'
then means afterwards, later

explanation.surface: A French artwork about an inspiring person that later includes a portrait titled 'Man with Sieve'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the verb (thou art), not painting: in French 'tu es'. Erato is the Muse of lyric poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eratosthenes, the Greek mathematician, devised the 'sieve' method for finding prime numbers, named after him.

clue.text: Parasites in hospital get young man very annoyed

parts.note: H is the map symbol and abbreviation for hospital
to anger a son is to get a young man very annoyed

explanation.surface: Freeloaders on a hospital ward making a young patient furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as an instruction: anger (make very annoyed) a son (young man).
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on attach themselves to someone for personal gain, living off them like parasites on a host.

clue.text: Happy church, always packed out, pretty much

indicators.note: pretty much means nearly all, so the final letter is cut away

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a packed-out venue is completely full

explanation.surface: A contented congregation whose church is nearly always full.
explanation.walkthrough: FULL loses its last letter to become FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful describes someone in good spirits, visibly glad and content.

clue.text: Remove boat parked on stretch of land

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a boat
a tract is a large area of land

explanation.surface: An instruction to take away a boat left on a piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece 'on' another means it sits above it, so SUB comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take something away from a total, so it means remove.

clue.text: Dropping Ecstasy, ease the undies off in Paris suburbs

indicators.note: something that has gone off has gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled
dropping something means letting it go, so that letter is taken out of the mix

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the raw letters, from which one E is removed

explanation.surface: A racy scene of drug-taking and undressing somewhere in the outskirts of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from EASE THE UNDIES, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauts-de-Seine is the French département covering the western suburbs of Paris, including La Défense.

clue.text: Meticulous precision of scaffolder picked up

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a rigger is a worker who erects scaffolding and lifting gear

explanation.surface: Praise for the careful exactness of a builder's work on the scaffolding.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling ends -OUR; in non-rhotic speech it sounds the same as RIGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour is strict thoroughness and exactness, the quality of being scrupulously careful.

clue.text: Without delay pay for catching cold

indicators.note: catching something means grabbing hold of it, so one word closes around a letter

parts.note: to atone for a wrong is to pay for it
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An urgent demand to pay the doctor for treating a cold straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: At once means immediately, with nothing postponed or deferred.

clue.text: Determined on parting from black American, touring divorce hub in confidence

indicators.note: touring means going all round a place, so these letters surround the city
parting from something means leaving it behind, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to be bent on something is to be determined on it
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
US is the abbreviation for American
Reno in Nevada was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: A secret story about someone set on leaving a Black American and heading off to the divorce capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno, Nevada, was once known as the divorce capital of the world because of its short residency rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Entre nous is French for 'between ourselves', said of something told privately, not to be repeated.

clue.text: Birds coming in to feather nest

indicators.note: coming in to something means being found inside it, so the letters are within the following words

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Birds flying in to line their nest with feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, a classic crossword word for a bird.

clue.text: Order the Chambers app?

definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: an electronic dictionary, E plus the short form DICT

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a British dictionary publisher; the question mark warns that an electronic dictionary is being written as E-DICT.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an authoritative proclamation issued by a ruler, a formal command.

clue.text: Cloth girl left on floor

indicators.note: in an across entry, sitting on something means coming after it, so the girl and left follow the floor

parts.note: FL is an abbreviation for floor
Anne is a girl's name
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A girl has left a cloth lying on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts girl and left after floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is a soft woven fabric, and in Britain also a small cloth for washing the face.

clue.text: Singer naked? Blow it!

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
naked means with nothing on, and nothing is O, giving O + ON

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at finding a singer performing undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow it!' sounds like a mild curse, but it is an instruction to play a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a woodwind instrument played by blowing through a double reed.

clue.text: Most fashionable chocolates, tiny boxes

indicators.note: something that boxes another encloses it, so the letters are inside the surrounding words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A trendy gift: little chocolates sold in boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest styles are the newest, so they are the most in vogue.

clue.text: Milk supplier in western university sacked

indicators.note: a place that is sacked is ransacked and left in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the raw letters
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A dairy supplier working at a western university gets fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse is a woman employed to breastfeed another person's baby, so she provides it with milk.
